title: Runtime parameter lint and recovery checklist for function-call JSON schemas
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a prescriptive runtime lint + recovery checklist and ship a lightweight validator that: (1) defines the recommended JSON Schema subset for function/tool parameters, (2) returns concise human-friendly error envelopes with actionable remediation hints, and (3) provides a compatibility layer for older client schemas. This ticket covers spec, validator prototype, test harness, and documentation for SDKs.
background: We have many ad-hoc tool/function JSON schemas in customer integrations. Runtime errors are often noisy and hard to remediate by non-technical users. Current validator variants across SDKs differ in message phrasing and recovery guidance, increasing support tickets and regressions during model/operator upgrades.
problem_statement: We need a single source-of-truth for: permitted schema constructs (to keep runtime validation cheap and predictable), standardized error code taxonomy and human-friendly remediation text, and a compatibility shim behavior for deprecated field names and coercion policies. Without this, customers see inconsistent errors, increased integration time, and higher incident churn.
goals: 1) Define a pragmatic JSON Schema subset for runtime (no $ref, no patternProperties, explicit types only). 2) Build a validator that emits structured error envelopes with suggested fixes. 3) Implement a compatibility mode that attempts safe repairs (coercion, alias mapping) and reports any repairs in the error envelope. 4) Provide clear docs and SDK examples.
non_goals: Full JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 support; complex cross-field validation rules beyond simple "if/then"; providing a universal coercion policy that changes semantics (we will only coerce safe transformations: numeric strings -> numbers, single-element arrays -> value when schema expects scalar and allow_coerce is enabled).
proposed_solution: 1) Spec: publish a 'Runtime Function Schema v1' spec (YAML+examples) that lists allowed keywords: type, properties, required, enum, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, items (fixed schemas only), additionalProperties (boolean). Ban $ref, patternProperties, dependencies, allOf/anyOf/oneOf except a limited union form explained in compatibility section. 2) Validator: implement a small Go/Python validator module used by runtime and SDKs. It returns a canonical error envelope with code, path, human_message, repair_actions (if any), and telemetry_tags. 3) Compatibility shim: when compatibility=true, validator will attempt limited repairs (aliases map, safe coercion). All repairs are reported with repair_actions and a repair_confidence score.
error_catalog: E_PARAM_MISSING: required parameter missing. human_message: 'Missing required field "<field>". Provide a value or remove the field from your call.' suggested_repair: 'Add value for <field> or mark it optional in schema.'

E_TYPE_MISMATCH: parameter type mismatch. human_message: 'Expected <expected_type> but got <received_type> for "<field>".' suggested_repair: 'Convert value to <expected_type>. When compatibility=true, the validator may coerce <received_type> to <expected_type> if safe.'

E_ENUM_MISMATCH: value not in allowed enum. human_message: 'Value "<value>" is not valid for "<field>". Allowed: <allowed_values>.' suggested_repair: 'Choose one of the allowed values or update schema to include new permitted value.'
E_NUM_OUT_OF_RANGE: numeric bounds violated. human_message: 'Value <value> for "<field>" out of range (<min> - <max>).' suggested_repair: 'Clamp value within bounds or change schema bounds.'
E_STRING_TOO_SHORT: string length below minLength. human_message: 'Provide a longer string for "<field>".' suggested_repair: 'Pad the string or relax minLength.'

E_ADDITIONAL_PROPERTY: unknown property present. human_message: 'Found unexpected field "<field>".' suggested_repair: 'Remove the field or add it to schema properties. In compatibility mode, unknown fields are preserved but flagged.'

E_SCHEMA_NOT_SUPPORTED: schema contained unsupported keywords (e.g. $ref). human_message: 'Schema uses unsupported construct "<keyword>".' suggested_repair: 'Refactor schema to use supported constructs or enable advanced-schema-mode (behind a runtime flag) if necessary.'

E_COERCION_FAILED: attempted coercion unsuccessful. human_message: 'Unable to coerce "<field>" from <from_type> to <to_type> safely.' suggested_repair: 'Provide correctly-typed value or update schema to accept the observed form.'
error_envelope_spec: The validator returns a top-level envelope (as JSON string) with fields: code (string), message (short), details (list of strings), path (JSON Pointer), suggested_fixes (list of strings), repairs_applied (list of strings), repair_confidence (0-1 string), telemetry_tags (list), compatible_mode (true/false as string). Example: { code: 'E_TYPE_MISMATCH', message: 'Expected integer', details: ['received string: "3"'], path: '/top_k', suggested_fixes: ['coerce string->int with compatibility=true'], repairs_applied: ['coerced_top_k=3'], repair_confidence: '0.9' }
compatibility_layer: Behavior when compatibility=true: 1) alias map applied: e.g., 'k' -> 'top_k', 'n_results' -> 'top_k'. 2) safe coercions: numeric strings -> integer/number, single-value arrays -> scalar (if scalar expected), true/false string -> boolean. 3) enums: case-insensitive match attempted for short strings. All changes are recorded in repairs_applied with a repair_confidence score. Compatibility mode must be opt-in by callers and disabled for strict validation in enterprise contexts.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit metric counters and traces for: validation.success, validation.failure.{code}, validation.repair.{code}, repair_confidence.histogram. Include schema_hash and runtime_version labels. Sample dashboard queries will be added to the runtime docs. Aim for <1ms median validation time for typical schemas.
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator core covering: required/optional fields, type coercion edge cases, enum matching, nested objects (depth up to 4), items validation for fixed-length arrays, and additionalProperties behavior. Fuzz tests: generate malformed payloads + deprecated schemas to ensure we don't silently change semantics. Integration: add end-to-end tests in runtime serving harness that assert error envelopes emitted to logs and that repaired requests are forwarded with repair metadata. Add SDK conformance tests for Python, Go, and JS.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec published in docs with examples. 2) Validator prototype merged and included in runtime image. 3) Integration tests pass in CI with <3 flaky runs in 1000 attempts. 4) SDKs include sample code and surface error envelopes to user. 5) Telemetry shows repair_rate <5% on a representative internal workload or else schema changes are required.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable validator in staging runtime with compatibility=true for internal teams and partner customers. Phase 2: enable strict validation for test deployments (compatibility=false) to catch schema issues. Phase 3: opt-in for public customers; advertise breaking change window and migration guide. Rollback: flip a runtime flag to disable validation entirely for emergency.
migration_guide: Guidance for SDK and customer migrations: 1) run compatibility mode locally to surface repair suggestions. 2) update caller code to conform to recommended schema. 3) opt into strict mode only after tests pass. Provide a small CLI tool (schema-lint) to scan repositories for common anti-patterns (use of $ref, patternProperties, deep anyOf).
open_questions: 1) Do we allow a limited oneOf form for discriminators? Proposal: allow oneOf only when discriminator field is explicit and all variants are closed objects.
2) How should we surface repairs across async streaming boundaries? Proposal: attach a validation header and include repairs in the initial response meta event for streaming calls.
3) Do we need per-tenant override for compatibility alias maps? Proposal: yes, via tenant config in Dedicated/Private.

4) Should the validator return HTTP 4xx for strict schema violations or 200 with error envelope in body? Proposal: 4xx for non-streaming control-plane calls; for streaming generation requests, emit a terminal error event with the envelope and close stream.
notes: Design favors predictable runtime performance and minimal surface area for validators. We will iterate on error phrasing with UX/Design. Keep repair heuristics conservative to avoid changing intended user input semantics.
decisions: Use a restricted JSON Schema subset to reduce validation cost and ambiguity.
Make compatibility mode opt-in and report all repairs explicitly.
Return structured error envelopes with suggested_fixes and repair_confidence for every validation result.
Keep coercions very conservative; prefer failing fast unless compatibility=true.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spec draft completed. Reviewed with API and Runtime teams; concerns raised about streaming semantics.
2026-03-05: Validator prototype (Go) implemented basic type checks and required-field detection. Benchmarked at ~0.6ms median for typical 3-field schemas.
2026-03-09: UX session with Developer Experience; agreed to include suggested_fixes keys and short remediation strings for each error code.
2026-03-12: Added compatibility alias map and simple coercion rules. Started integration tests for streaming initial-meta event behavior.
